problems.problem: Bottle contact with the surface remains ambiguous. The product_base_y (1255) is 87.2% of canvas height (1440), but the shadow.offset_y (5) is still slightly detached from the bottle base, violating contact shadow physics. The burgundy floor lacks visible texture or tonal transition to confirm a raised tabletop, making the bottle appear to float.

Typography remains disconnected from the product. The title ("J'adore") and logo ("Dior") are placed in the upper right, creating a split visual flow between the bottle (left) and text (right). The product occupies 59% of canvas height (850/1440), which is within range, but the text placement lacks integration with the bottle's form.

Compared to professional references (e.g., Tom Ford Figue with fig integration, Byredo Rose of No Man's Land with bold graphic elements), the composition lacks a cohesive visual narrative. The burgundy background and diagonal shadow are generic, failing to create the thematic depth seen in luxury campaigns.

changes.value: Empty deep burgundy red studio with matte wine-red paper floor and wall, large diagonal architectural shadow from upper right, flat geometric color fields, editorial still-life set, clear foreground left, subtle texture on floor surface
